playbooks.title: Site-wide robotic stoppage with AGV synchronization loss
playbooks.user_facing_summary: Use this response pattern when operators report that robots or AGVs are stopped, nothing is moving, the small sort is not running, or the robotic system is not responding. Confirm the scope and observable system state, investigate service and application health, restore the named robotic service or gateway through an approved procedure, correct residual AGV synchronization issues, and validate API and operational recovery.
playbooks.playbook_goal: Restore stable robotic and sort operation by distinguishing a site-wide control-system or service interruption from a localized AGV condition, then validating service responsiveness, AGV state, and resumed automated operation.
observed_entry_symptoms: Operators reported that nothing was moving.
The robotic system was reported as not responding.
The small sort was not running.
Multiple bots were reported as not moving in different areas.
Totes could not be removed from the hospital workflow.
The RMS/HMI appeared mostly blank and displayed a message reported as '.NET Control not created.'
AGVs were reported as out of sync.

playbooks.confidence_reason: The packet contains direct source artifacts and case comments covering the symptom pattern, Event Viewer evidence, service recovery, RMS AGV correction, API validation, and operational recovery. Exact recovery commands and the definitive causal chain are intentionally not inferred.

nodes.title: Confirm the observable scope of the stoppage
nodes.intent: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide or broad robotic stoppage with abnormal control-system presentation rather than an isolated robot issue.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide or broad robotic stoppage with abnormal control-system presentation rather than an isolated robot issue.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to ask the site which affected areas or workflows are stopped, whether multiple robots are stationary, and whether automated sorting or hospital tote removal is affected; also inspect the RMS/HMI overview for a normally populated versus mostly blank operational display and any readable system or AGV error indicators.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident began with reports that nothing was moving, the small sort was not running, and the robotic system was not responding; RMS screenshots showed an abnormal mostly blank presentation.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to ask the site which affected areas or workflows are stopped, whether multiple robots are stationary, and whether automated sorting or hospital tote removal is affected; also inspect the RMS/HMI overview for a normally populated versus mostly blank operational display and any readable system or AGV error indicators.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or support user confirms through site interview and the RMS/HMI view whether multiple robots or areas are stopped, the small sort or hospital workflow is affected, and the RMS page is populated normally. Unhealthy signals are broad non-movement, robotic-system nonresponse, or a mostly blank RMS page with an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message. Healthy signals are localized impact with otherwise normal fleet presentation. Inconclusive signals are an unclear scope report, unreadable RMS display, or unavailable site confirmation.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: RMS screenshots show ACB System 1 - RMS with a mostly blank panel and an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message; page 5.
Case comments and Teams messages record site reports that nothing was moving, the robotic system was not responding, and hospital totes could not be removed; pages 2 and 25.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet contains a site-wide stoppage report and a blank RMS/system-status presentation.

healthy_indicators: Site reports only a localized issue.
RMS overview is populated and shows normal system presentation.
Other automated areas continue operating.
unhealthy_indicators: Multiple areas or robots are stopped.
Nothing is moving or the robotic system is not responding.
Small sort or hospital workflow is unavailable.
RMS main panel is mostly blank or shows the apparent '.NET Control not created.' message.
inconclusive_indicators: Only one robot is reported stopped.
The RMS image or error sections cannot be read.
The site cannot confirm whether the stoppage is broad or localized.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If the scope cannot be confirmed or the evidence is limited to an unreadable interface, leave this path for retriage rather than assuming a system-wide service fault.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Reports stated that 4-6 bots were not moving, hospital totes could not be removed, and nothing was moving.
RMS page was mostly blank and displayed an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message.

nodes.primary_action: Ask the site to confirm which areas/workflows are stopped (including whether the small sort and hospital tote removal are affected) and inspect the RMS overview presentation to determine whether the display is normally populated versus mostly blank with the reported “.NET Control not created.” message.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation of scope: broad/site-wide vs localized impact (multiple robots/areas stopped vs only one robot/area).
Whether small sort operation is stopped and whether hospital tote removal is impacted.
RMS overview screenshot/state: normally populated vs mostly blank; any readable system/AGV error indicator sections; whether the “.NET Control not created.” message is present/readable.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Impact is localized (not broad) and the RMS overview is populated and shows normal system presentation; automated areas not in the reported scope continue operating normally.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Broad stoppage with abnormal control-system presentation: multiple areas/robots appear stopped or the robotic system is not responding; small sort/hospital workflow unavailable; RMS main panel mostly blank and shows an apparent “.NET Control not created.” message.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Scope cannot be confirmed (unclear broad vs localized), RMS image/error sections are unreadable, or site confirmation is unavailable/incomplete.

optional_corroboration.note: If the site cannot confirm scope, avoid assuming service failure based solely on a partially readable RMS blank page—proceed via the service-failure evidence path only after scope is at least tentatively broad or RMS presentation remains abnormal.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use this node to prevent premature service recovery assumptions. Treat the RMS blank/“.NET Control not created.” observation as a scope indicator, not a confirmed root cause. Branch only after collecting site scope confirmation and verifying whether the RMS overview is normally populated versus mostly blank.

nodes.goal: Determine whether Windows evidence indicates an OptiSweep service termination or clustered WCSWebApplication/application errors that correlate with the broad stoppage.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for the named OptiSweep service and WCSWebApplication, including Service Control Manager termination events, the visible Event 7031 category, clustered application errors, and the WCSWebApplication Event 20102 failed-command evidence, while preserving timestamps and uncertainty.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source shows OptiSweep Event 7031 termination evidence and clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries around 6:35-6:36 AM.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for the named OptiSweep service and WCSWebApplication, including Service Control Manager termination events, the visible Event 7031 category, clustered application errors, and the WCSWebApplication Event 20102 failed-command evidence, while preserving timestamps and uncertainty.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1, L2, or L3 support reviews Windows Event Viewer. Unhealthy signals are a System-log Service Control Manager event showing OptiSweep terminated unexpectedly, or Application-log WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries clustered around the reported interruption, including the visible Event ID 20102 failed database-command evidence. Healthy signals are no relevant service termination or clustered application errors. Inconclusive signals are unavailable logs, ambiguous timestamps, or errors without a credible temporal relationship to the stoppage.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Incident artifacts show Windows Event Viewer Application and System logs, including WCSWebApplication errors and OptiSweep Event 7031; pages 27-29.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: Event Viewer artifacts directly show Service Control Manager Event 7031 and clustered application errors.
The packet names OptiSweep and WCSWebApplication and documents their abnormal events.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a specific Event Viewer event-to-service recovery mapping beyond the named capability.
healthy_indicators: No relevant OptiSweep termination event is present in the incident window.
No clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries are present.
The reviewed service and application evidence is temporally unrelated to the reported symptoms.
unhealthy_indicators: Service Control Manager Event 7031 states that OptiSweep terminated unexpectedly.
Application-log entries show clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error events around the stoppage.
WCSWebApplication Event 20102 shows a failed database command near the interruption.
inconclusive_indicators: Event logs are unavailable or incomplete.
The event timestamp cannot be aligned with the symptom report.
The event text is unreadable or only indicates a generic warning.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Event 7031 states that the OptiSweep service terminated unexpectedly and that Windows planned a restart.

nodes.primary_action: Review Windows Event Viewer (System/Application) for OptiSweep termination evidence and clustered WCSWebApplication/application errors around the reported interruption window, preserving timestamps and uncertainty.
evidence_to_collect: Windows Event Viewer System log evidence for OptiSweep termination/restart (including Service Control Manager Event 7031 text).
Windows Event Viewer Application log evidence for WCSWebApplication/Application Error clusters around the stoppage window.
Whether Event ID 20102 (WCSWebApplication failed database command) is present near the interruption timeline.
Exact timestamps for correlation (and note if they cannot be credibly aligned to symptoms).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: No relevant OptiSweep termination event and no clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries temporally related to the stoppage.

nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Logs unavailable/incomplete, timestamps ambiguous, or errors cannot be aligned credibly to the stoppage window.

nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness through the incident-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API endpoint, inspect returned AGV records without treating the client schema warning as a confirmed service failure, and corroborate with Ignition Systems Overview and Windows Services when those surfaces are available.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source defines GetAgvStatuses as a post-restart responsiveness check and shows HTTP 200 with returned AGV records, while also documenting Ignition and Windows Services checks.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness through the incident-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API endpoint, inspect returned AGV records without treating the client schema warning as a confirmed service failure, and corroborate with Ignition Systems Overview and Windows Services when those surfaces are available.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1, L2, or L3 support checks the named OptiSweep/WCS API and, where applicable, the Ignition Systems Overview and Windows Services state. Healthy signals are a successful GetAgvStatuses response with returned AGV records, an available gateway status page, and a Running OptiSweep service. Unhealthy signals are no API response, unavailable gateway, or a stopped or repeatedly failing service. Inconclusive signals are HTTP success with unclear data validity, such as the observed schema warning, or a status page without confirmation of current service responsiveness.

nodes.title: Determine whether residual AGV synchronization issues remain
nodes.intent: Identify whether individual AGVs remain out of sync after service responsiveness has returned.
nodes.goal: Identify whether individual AGVs remain out of sync after service responsiveness has returned.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or map view for out-of-sync AGVs and to corroborate relevant robot state through the read-only robotics database view in SQL Server Management Studio or the GetAgvStatuses response; the procedure must define how to distinguish residual synchronization problems from normal charging, queueing, or exchange states.
nodes.source_supported_description: After the OptiSweep reset, RMS was used to locate and correct AGVs that remained out of sync; a separate artifact shows read-only SSMS inspection of AGV states.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or map view for out-of-sync AGVs and to corroborate relevant robot state through the read-only robotics database view in SQL Server Management Studio or the GetAgvStatuses response; the procedure must define how to distinguish residual synchronization problems from normal charging, queueing, or exchange states.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator or support user reviews the RMS fleet or map view and, where available to authorized remote support, corroborates the AGV state through the incident-evidenced SSMS robotics view or API response. Unhealthy signals are AGVs still marked out of sync, inconsistent with the expected fleet state, or not participating normally after service recovery. Healthy signals are no residual out-of-sync AGVs and a coherent fleet view. Inconclusive signals are unreadable AGV state, ambiguous waiting or charging states, or an API response whose records cannot be interpreted.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Case comments state that RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs; page 26.
A readable artifact visibly shows SQL Server Management Studio with robotics-related AGV state results; page 24.
The packet includes GetAgvStatuses response records and status values; page 17.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source describes locating individual out-of-sync AGVs and includes backend AGV state evidence.
The RMS interface includes AGV error sections and the incident evidence includes AGV status and error-related records.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not define the authoritative state value that means out of sync.
The SQL artifact does not provide a validated interpretation for each displayed queue, charging, exchange, or waiting state.
healthy_indicators: RMS shows the expected fleet without residual out-of-sync indicators.
Read-only state evidence is coherent with the expected operational state.
No residual AGV errors or mismatched roster states are identified.
unhealthy_indicators: One or more AGVs remain reported as out of sync.
RMS and the corroborating status evidence disagree about AGV membership or state.
AGV error or abnormal-state indicators remain after service recovery.
inconclusive_indicators: The RMS map or AGV error sections are unreadable.
The API returns records but their state meaning is unclear.
The SSMS results show waiting, charging, staging, or exchange states without a validated interpretation.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: RMS was used to locate AGVs that were out of sync and fix them individually.
SQL Server Management Studio visibly showed robotics-related AGV state results.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect for residual residual AGV out-of-sync/synchronization issues using RMS fleet/map status and corroborate AGV state via WCS/robotics read-only SSMS and/or GetAgvStatuses data, and distinguish residual sync problems from normal charging/queueing/exchange states.
evidence_to_collect: RMS fleet/map indications of AGVs remaining out of sync (and whether any AGV error sections are visible/readable).
Read-only SSMS robotics state evidence used to interpret robot roster/location state; identify any devices still inconsistent with expected post-recovery behavior.
GetAgvStatuses record set interpretation (only if records are interpretable) to corroborate or resolve ambiguities from RMS view.
Evidence classification: out-of-sync vs normal queueing/charging/exchange waiting states (note that the authoritative state meaning may require SME clarification if not present in the packet).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: No residual out-of-sync indicators: RMS shows expected fleet without residual mismatches, and read-only robotics/API state is coherent with normal operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Residual synchronization problems remain: one or more AGVs still marked out of sync or roster/state mismatch persists and corroboration agrees it’s abnormal.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS sections unreadable, API records present but state meaning unclear, or SSMS outputs show states (waiting/charging/exchange) without validated mapping to “out of sync.”
nodes.generated_guidance: Prefer WCS/SSMS read-only state truth to interpret synchronization. If the ontology mapping for the exact “out of sync” value is missing/unclear, flag a catalog/interpretation gap and avoid physical actions; proceed using the available next gates (correction or validation/escalation).

nodes.intent: Use the authorized RMS recovery procedure to correct individually identified out-of-sync AGVs after the control service is responsive.
nodes.goal: Use the authorized RMS recovery procedure to correct individually identified out-of-sync AGVs after the control service is responsive.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized RMS handling of an individually identified out-of-sync AGV, including safety preconditions, role limits, identification of the affected asset, correction completion criteria, and boundaries for physical AGV recovery or unsupported state changes.
nodes.source_supported_description: The historical response used RMS to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs one by one after resetting OptiSweep.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized RMS handling of an individually identified out-of-sync AGV, including safety preconditions, role limits, identification of the affected asset, correction completion criteria, and boundaries for physical AGV recovery or unsupported state changes.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized operator or support role records that the identified AGV synchronization corrections are complete. Progress is indicated by the affected AGV no longer appearing out of sync in the RMS or corroborating state view. Failure is indicated by an AGV remaining out of sync, becoming unavailable, or requiring an unsupported physical or configuration action. Inconclusive status means the correction result cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source states that RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs individually; page 26.

ontology_gaps: The source does not describe the exact RMS correction operation or define when physical AGV recovery is required.
healthy_indicators: Each identified AGV is no longer represented as out of sync.
The RMS fleet view is coherent after the authorized correction.
No new AGV error or safety condition is introduced.
unhealthy_indicators: An identified AGV remains out of sync after the approved correction.
The AGV cannot be safely or consistently represented in the RMS state.
Correction requires an operation outside the authorized role or source-supported procedure.
inconclusive_indicators: RMS state does not refresh or is unreadable.
The source state and displayed state cannot be correlated.
The correction appears complete but automated operation has not yet been validated.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Stop if the identified AGV requires physical handling, an E-stop decision, configuration change, database mutation, or another action not covered by the authorized procedure.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: After resetting OptiSweep, RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs individually.

nodes.primary_action: Use the authorized RMS recovery procedure to correct individually identified out-of-sync AGVs, then confirm in RMS/corroborating state views that each AGV no longer appears out of sync.
evidence_to_collect: Identification of the affected AGVs that are out of sync (from node_5 evidence).
Evidence of completion: each corrected AGV no longer appears out of sync in RMS (and corroborating state view if available).
Any new/unexpected safety conditions or AGV errors introduced by the correction (should not happen per expected outcomes).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Each identified AGV is no longer represented as out of sync and fleet view is coherent after correction.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An AGV remains out of sync after approved correction, becomes unavailable/inconsistent in RMS state, or correction requires physical handling/unsupported actions.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS state does not refresh or cannot be correlated to source state; correction appears complete but automated operation validation not yet performed.
nodes.generated_guidance: Stop if correction requires physical AGV handling, E-stop decision, configuration change, or DB mutation outside authorized scope. After correction, proceed to stable operation validation gate.
nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Authorized RMS correction step for residual synchronization issues.

linked_runbooks.purpose: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) live read-only database surface to inspect robotics-related AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped. Compare the populated SSMS State results with the live RMS / fleet status UI; the listed state values do not independently establish a fault.

linked_runbooks.title: Remove/Recover a specific AGV by robot ID using OptiSweep→Geek API requests
linked_runbooks.purpose: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API client to send a Geek request to remove a specified AGV from the system (RemoveAgv) or re-add it (RecoverAGV). Both API actions require the target robot ID.

nodes.trigger_condition: The authorized operator or support role records that the identified AGV synchronization corrections are complete. Progress is indicated by the affected AGV no longer appearing out of sync in the RMS or corroborating state view. Failure is indicated by an AGV remaining out of sync, becoming unavailable, or requiring an unsupported physical or configuration action. Inconclusive status means the correction result cannot be confirmed.

selected_procedure.title: Recover From AGV Fault During Exchange (RMS E-stop, remove faulted AGV, backfill, introduce new tote + empty AGV)
selected_procedure.purpose: Restore exchange flow after an AGV faults while leaving by stopping RMS, removing the faulted AGV from the RMS, optionally removing the trailing AGV if it does not backfill, then introducing a new tote and placing an empty AGV in the affected zone.

safety_checks: Perform an RMS E-stop as the first recovery action for this fault scenario.
nodes.success_confirmation: Faulted AGV is removed from RMS.
nodes.failure_boundary: Trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described.

runbook_execution_result.success: Faulted AGV is removed from RMS.
runbook_execution_result.failure: Trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described.

nodes.title: Validate stable automated operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that service responsiveness, AGV state, and the affected automated workflows have recovered sufficiently to declare the technical response successful.
nodes.goal: Confirm that service responsiveness, AGV state, and the affected automated workflows have recovered sufficiently to declare the technical response successful.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep service state, repeat the GetAgvStatuses responsiveness check, review RMS fleet state for residual synchronization issues, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement and the affected sort or bag-out workflow remain operational before declaring recovery.
nodes.source_supported_description: The historical response reported resumed auto bag-out after service reset and RMS correction, with API and service-state evidence used as validation.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep service state, repeat the GetAgvStatuses responsiveness check, review RMS fleet state for residual synchronization issues, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement and the affected sort or bag-out workflow remain operational before declaring recovery.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator confirms that automated movement and the affected sort workflow have resumed, while support confirms service/API responsiveness and no residual out-of-sync AGVs in the available status views. Healthy signals are resumed auto bag-out or automated operation, normal or coherent AGV status, and continued service responsiveness. Unhealthy signals are renewed non-movement, inability to complete the affected workflow, repeated service termination, or residual AGV synchronization issues. Inconclusive signals are only a service-running display, a single HTTP 200 response with unresolved data ambiguity, or recovery of one workflow without confirmation of broader operation.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source states that RMS was used to correct AGVs and that the site then resumed auto bag-out; page 26.
The source records GetAgvStatuses as the post-restart validation check and shows HTTP 200 with returned records; pages 17-18.
Windows Services showed OptiSweep in a Running state; page 19.
Case evidence states that the site resumed auto bag-out and was later reported as running; page 26 and close comment.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet documents site-wide stoppage and later resumed automated operation.
GetAgvStatuses was explicitly used as a post-restart validation check.
RMS was used to locate and correct out-of-sync AGVs.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not define a duration or monitoring interval for stable recovery.
The source confirms resumed auto bag-out but does not quantify whether every site function was restored.
healthy_indicators: GetAgvStatuses continues to return usable AGV records.
OptiSweep remains Running.
RMS shows no residual out-of-sync AGVs.
The site confirms automated movement and the affected sort or bag-out workflow have resumed.
unhealthy_indicators: Robots stop again or nothing is moving.
The affected sort or bag-out workflow remains unavailable.
OptiSweep terminates again or API responsiveness is lost.
Residual out-of-sync AGVs remain after correction.
inconclusive_indicators: Only the service Running state is confirmed.
The API returns HTTP 200 but the response schema warning remains unresolved.
The site reports one workflow resumed without confirming broader automated operation.
RMS status is unavailable or stale.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If validation fails after the authorized recovery and AGV correction path, stop and prepare an evidence-based technical handoff rather than repeating unsupported recovery actions.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Instructions required confirming OptiSweep response with a Get Statuses request before releasing the E-stop.
After correcting out-of-sync AGVs, the site resumed the auto bag-out procedure.

nodes.primary_action: Validate stable automated operation after service responsiveness and residual AGV correction: confirm the site observes resumed automated movement and the affected workflow (e.g., auto bag-out/sort operation) continues working.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation that automated movement resumed and the affected workflow (sort or bag-out) remains operational and continues moving.
Support confirmation that GetAgvStatuses continues to return usable AGV records and OptiSweep remains Running (from previously validated evidence, plus any repeat check performed).
RMS view shows no residual out-of-sync AGVs and fleet status appears coherent (if readable).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Stable recovery: automated movement/workflow resumed and remains running; service/API responsiveness still good; no residual out-of-sync AGVs in available status views.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Validation fails: renewed non-movement, workflow remains unavailable, repeated service termination or lost API responsiveness, or residual out-of-sync AGVs remain.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only partial evidence exists (e.g., service Running but no operational workflow confirmation; or HTTP 200 with unresolved schema ambiguity; or RMS status stale/unavailable).
nodes.generated_guidance: Declare success only when both control-path responsiveness and site-observed workflow resumption agree. If validation fails, do not repeat recovery actions blindly—prepare a handoff package.

ontology_evidence.text: Capability agv_active_errors: Confirm whether AGVs/robots currently have active error or fault state.. Not for: Physical bump recovery steps (use agv_physical_recovery); Ignition OPC alone; tote NoRead.. Surfaces: rms_ui, wcs_sql, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. Support contract: {}. playbooks.title: AMR pairing failure with abnormal fleet roster or mapping state
playbooks.user_facing_summary: Use this path when a site reports that an ACB or zone cannot obtain an AMR pair, multiple AMRs route unexpectedly, or the system appears down after an AMR replacement or add/remove event.
playbooks.playbook_goal: Determine whether the pairing failure is associated with an abnormal AMR roster or mapping state, use an authorized site-side isolation or removal procedure when supported, and confirm that normal pairing and operation return.
observed_entry_symptoms: A site reports that an ACB or affected zone cannot get a pair.
The ACB system is described as down or production is seriously impacted.
Replacement AMRs reportedly route to the hospital lane instead of supporting the affected workflow.
An AMR was previously reported with low battery or in an abnormal physical location.
The issue follows an AMR replacement, add, or remove activity.
support_user_language_examples: AMRs are going to the hospital
The robot was replaced and nothing is pairing
AGV was added but it is not getting a task
Robots are not working after an add/remove
A site reports that an ACB or affected
The ACB system is described as down or production is seriously impacted
Replacement AMRs reportedly route to the hospital lane
An AMR was previously reported with low battery
The issue follows an AMR replacement, add, or remove activity
zone unable to get a pair
every AMR goes to the hospital
playbooks.confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear observable symptom, a named RMS surface, discussion of possible roster/add-remove behavior, a source-supported site removal action, and reported recovery. Confidence is limited because the RMS details are partly unreadable, recovery was reported rather than independently measured, and the source contains inconsistent ACB/ECB naming.

nodes.title: Confirm the observable pairing and routing pattern
nodes.intent: Determine whether the site is experiencing an active pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or behavior after a replacement or add/remove event.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the site is experiencing an active pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or behavior after a replacement or add/remove event.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to interview the site about the affected zone's pairing availability, intended AMR routing, recent replacement or add/remove activity, and current physical robot behavior; this is an evidence-collection and interpretation aid, not a case-intake procedure.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records site-reported inability to get a pair, replacement AMRs going to the hospital lane, and earlier low-battery and robot-location circumstances.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to interview the site about the affected zone's pairing availability, intended AMR routing, recent replacement or add/remove activity, and current physical robot behavior; this is an evidence-collection and interpretation aid, not a case-intake procedure.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support confirms through site interview or visual observation whether the affected zone cannot obtain a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane instead of the intended workflow, and whether the pattern followed an AMR replacement or add/remove event. Healthy means pairing and intended routing are available; unhealthy means pairing remains unavailable or multiple AMRs show the reported abnormal routing; inconclusive means the site cannot confirm the affected workflow, timing, or current behavior.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support messages record a phone conversation with the site and site-reported pairing, low-battery, replacement, and hospital-lane behavior (case_228723:page_1; case_228723:page_2).

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source describes replacement/add activity, a robot reportedly not mapped, and abnormal routing.

ontology_gaps: No ontology-backed source mapping is provided for interpreting the phrase 'unable to get a pair' from the site interview alone.
healthy_indicators: Site reports that the affected workflow can obtain a pair.
AMRs are routing to the intended workflow rather than uniformly to the hospital lane.
unhealthy_indicators: Site confirms the affected zone still cannot obtain a pair.
Multiple replacement AMRs continue routing to the hospital lane.
A recent add/remove or replacement event coincides with the current failure.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot reproduce the pairing failure.
The affected workflow or current robot behavior cannot be identified.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site reported that the affected zone was unable to get a pair.
Site reported an earlier low-battery AMR issue and replacement AMRs going to the hospital lane.

match_gaps: Limited domain-term overlap between placeholder and runbook.
Placeholder wording differs materially from matched runbook title.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm with the site (interview and/or immediate physical observation) whether the affected zone can’t obtain a pair and whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane after the recent add/remove or replacement event.
evidence_to_collect: Affected zone/workflow identifier (as described by the site/operator).
Whether pairing is currently unavailable (site-confirmed).
Observed/confirmed routing behavior (e.g., AMRs going to hospital lane vs intended workflow).
Timing context: whether the symptom began after an AMR replacement or add/remove activity.
Physical behavior notes of the replacement/new AMR(s) (what the site can see on the floor).
What the site believes the “unable to get a pair” condition specifically means in their UI/workflow (if they can point to it).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The site operator or L1 support confirms pairing is available for the affected workflow and AMRs route to the intended workflow rather than consistently to the hospital lane.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The site operator or L1 support confirms the affected zone/workflow still cannot obtain a pair and/or multiple replacement AMRs continue routing to the hospital lane, coinciding with the recent replacement/add/remove context.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The site cannot reproduce the issue, cannot identify the affected workflow/robots, or cannot confirm current pairing/routing behavior or timing relative to the replacement/add/remove event.
nodes.generated_guidance: Treat the site report as the trigger for evidence collection and interpretation. Do not infer low-battery or a specific roster/mapping fault from the interview alone; the goal here is only to confirm that the observable pairing and routing pattern is active and tied to the recent replacement/add/remove activity.

nodes.title: Check fleet roster and mapping state
nodes.intent: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.
nodes.goal: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for roster membership, mapping, location, and exception indicators associated with the affected workflow, and to interpret whether the displayed state is consistent with normal pairing.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source identifies RMS as the system used to view robot status and states that a removed robot was shown as not mapped; the artifact shows red-highlighted RMS table entries.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for roster membership, mapping, location, and exception indicators associated with the affected workflow, and to interpret whether the displayed state is consistent with normal pairing.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support inspects the RMS fleet or robot status view. Healthy means the relevant robot membership, mapping, and status appear consistent with the intended operating area; unhealthy means a robot is shown as not mapped, missing, duplicated, abnormal, or highlighted as an exception; inconclusive means the RMS view is unreadable, unavailable, or does not identify the relevant robot state.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet includes readable context identifying RMS screenshots and an artifact showing RMS robot status tables with red-highlighted entries (case_228723:page_6).

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The case states that the removed robot was shown as not mapped and includes RMS status-table evidence.

ontology_gaps: The supplied incident evidence does not provide readable RMS field names or a validated mapping from the red table entries to a specific pairing state.
healthy_indicators: RMS shows the relevant robot roster and mapping as consistent with the operating area.
No relevant exception or abnormal membership indicator remains.
unhealthy_indicators: RMS shows a relevant robot as not mapped or otherwise abnormal.
RMS displays exception-highlighted robot or fleet entries associated with the affected workflow.
inconclusive_indicators: RMS status text or table values cannot be read reliably.
The displayed abnormal entry cannot be correlated with the affected workflow.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: RMS robot status tables show red-highlighted entries; exact values are unreadable.
Resolution details state that the removed robot was shown as not mapped.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect RMS fleet/robot status views to determine whether the roster/mapping state is abnormal for the affected workflow (e.g., missing/not mapped, exception-highlighted, or otherwise inconsistent membership).
evidence_to_collect: RMS evidence of the relevant robot membership/mapping for the affected workflow (as identified by the site interview).
Whether any robot is shown as not mapped / missing / abnormal in RMS.
Any exception-highlighted entries in RMS that appear tied to the affected workflow.
Whether the displayed abnormal entry can be correlated to the affected workflow described in the site report.
RMS readability status (if the relevant table values/fields cannot be read).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: RMS shows roster/mapping consistent with normal operation for the affected workflow; no abnormal/unmapped/exception indicators remain for the relevant robot(s).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: RMS shows abnormal roster/mapping for relevant robot(s) (e.g., a robot shown as not mapped, missing, duplicated, or exception-highlighted and correlating to the affected workflow).
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS state is unreadable/unavailable or the abnormal entry cannot be reliably correlated to the affected workflow.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: RMS robot status tables show red-highlighted entries; exact values are unreadable.
Resolution details state that the removed robot was shown as not mapped.

linked_runbooks.title: Check RMS fleet status for AGVs in shutdown queues and zone cycling
linked_runbooks.purpose: Use the RMS / fleet status UI to verify that AGVs are held in shutdown queues (shutdown state), then cycle into their assigned zones (4 zones) after startup, consistent with the system state model described in the segment.

fields.name: SortGuid
fields.meaning: Sort identifier during which the error occurred.

technical_field_mapping.availability: Validated read-only WCS SQL suggestions are available as corroboration.

nodes.question: Determine whether RMS shows an abnormal robot membership, mapping, or status condition that could explain the pairing failure.

runbook_execution_result.success: In RMS, AGVs expected to be in shutdown are shown in shutdown queues/shutdown state.
runbook_execution_result.failure: AGVs remain in shutdown queues/shutdown state without transitioning into their assigned zones when startup is expected.

node_interpretation_mapping.success: RMS shows normal relevant roster/mapping; suspected pattern not indicated.
node_interpretation_mapping.failure: RMS indicates an unmapped/abnormal/inconsistent robot roster/mapping state correlated to the affected workflow.
node_interpretation_mapping.inconclusive: RMS is unreadable/unavailable or abnormal entry cannot be correlated to the affected workflow.

nodes.title: Use an authorized site-side robot isolation or removal path
nodes.intent: If an abnormal roster or mapping condition is supported, use the approved site procedure to isolate or remove the affected robot from the operating system and place it in a safe non-operational state.
nodes.goal: If an abnormal roster or mapping condition is supported, use the approved site procedure to isolate or remove the affected robot from the operating system and place it in a safe non-operational state.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AGV physical isolation and system removal, including safety prerequisites, handling of a robot in an abnormal location, charger placement, and confirmation of the corresponding RMS state; exact removal or handling steps belong in the runbook.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident reports site-side removal of a robot from the system and placement on a charger, followed by reported system recovery.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AGV physical isolation and system removal, including safety prerequisites, handling of a robot in an abnormal location, charger placement, and confirmation of the corresponding RMS state; exact removal or handling steps belong in the runbook.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized site operator observes that the identified robot has been removed or isolated from active operation and placed in the reported safe state, such as charging, without creating a new physical hazard. Successful completion is confirmed by the site; failure or uncertainty means the robot cannot be safely isolated, the system-side state is unclear, or the action is outside the executor's authorization.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source includes RMS screenshots and a visible note that the site removed a robot from the system (case_228723:page_6).

ontology_gaps: The packet does not specify the approved remove/add procedure, authorization boundary, or exact system-side confirmation criteria.
healthy_indicators: Authorized site personnel confirm the affected robot is safely isolated and no longer participating in active operation.
unhealthy_indicators: The robot remains active, obstructed, or associated with the abnormal roster state.
The system continues to exhibit the pairing failure after the supported isolation action.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot confirm the robot's physical state or the corresponding RMS state.
The source-supported action cannot be performed safely or by an authorized role.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Stop if physical access, safety conditions, authorization, or system-side state cannot be confirmed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site removed the robot from the system, placed it on a charger, and reported that the system began functioning again.

nodes.primary_action: If an abnormal roster/mapping condition is supported, isolate/remove the affected robot using the authorized site-side physical action path and place it into a safe non-operational state (e.g., charging) without creating hazards; then confirm the corresponding RMS state as feasible.
evidence_to_collect: Safety prerequisites and authorization status for the site/operator performing physical handling.
Physical state confirmation: robot removed/isolated and placed into safe non-operational state (such as charging).
Whether the physical handling created any new hazard or obstruction.
Any site-observed change to pairing/operation immediately after completion.
Feasibility of confirming corresponding RMS state (if it can be checked).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Authorized site personnel confirm the robot is safely isolated/removed from active operation and placed in the intended safe state without creating a new physical hazard.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Robot remains active/obstructed or still associated with the abnormal roster state, and pairing failure continues after the supported action.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The site cannot confirm physical state or corresponding RMS state; or the action cannot be performed safely/within authorization.
nodes.generated_guidance: Stop if physical access, safety conditions, authorization, or system-side state cannot be confirmed. Do not invent the specific removal/charger steps—use the canonical approved site procedure for authorized isolation/removal.

ontology_evidence.evidence_text: Node aligns with on-site AGV add/remove/bump recovery coordination; healthy = robot recovered on floor and roster/map healthy; inconclusive when floor/system-side state cannot be confirmed.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Physical isolation/removal is allowed only when the supported roster/mapping abnormality exists; ensure safety and authorization boundaries are satisfied.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Site removed the robot from the system, placed it on a charger, and reported that the system began functioning again.

nodes.trigger_condition: The authorized site operator observes that the identified robot has been removed or isolated from active operation and placed in the reported safe state, such as charging, without creating a new physical hazard. Successful completion is confirmed by the site; failure or uncertainty means the robot cannot be safely isolated, the system-side state is unclear, or the action is outside the executor's authorization.
nodes.failure_boundary: Stop at the documented failure condition and escalate; do not invent a recovery path.

nodes.title: Confirm pairing and operational stability
nodes.intent: Determine whether the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized robot isolation or removal action.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized robot isolation or removal action.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate pairing availability through site observation and to review the RMS fleet or robot status view for persistent abnormal membership, mapping, or exception indicators during a defined monitoring period.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that the system began functioning after robot removal and remained operational during approximately ten minutes of monitoring, while acknowledging that the recovery was not independently validated by readable RMS data.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate pairing availability through site observation and to review the RMS fleet or robot status view for persistent abnormal membership, mapping, or exception indicators during a defined monitoring period.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator confirms that the affected workflow can obtain a pair and that AMRs are operating as expected; where available, the operator or L1 support checks the RMS fleet view for the abnormal entry to be absent or no longer active. Healthy means pairing resumes and operation remains stable during observation; unhealthy means pairing remains unavailable, AMRs continue routing abnormally, or the abnormal RMS state persists; inconclusive means recovery is only reported administratively or the RMS details cannot be read.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source reports that the site believed the system was working and that support remained on the call to monitor it (case_228723:page_7).
The recovery evidence includes embedded RMS screenshots associated with the report that the system remained operational (case_228723:page_10).

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source uses RMS screenshots and reports continued operation after robot removal, but does not provide independently readable final roster values.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not define a validated live RMS success state or an independent telemetry-based recovery check.
healthy_indicators: Site confirms that the affected workflow can obtain a pair.
AMRs no longer uniformly route to the hospital lane.
RMS no longer shows the relevant abnormal roster or mapping indication.
Operation remains stable during monitoring.
unhealthy_indicators: The affected workflow still cannot obtain a pair.
AMRs continue routing to the hospital lane unexpectedly.
RMS continues to show a relevant unmapped or abnormal robot state.
inconclusive_indicators: Recovery is stated only in a case comment or message without direct operational confirmation.
The RMS screenshots do not show readable final status details.
The system works briefly but stable monitoring is not completed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site believed removal may have fixed the issue and support monitored operation.
System reportedly began functioning again and remained operational during approximately ten minutes of monitoring.

nodes.primary_action: Validate recovery by confirming pairing availability and operational stability after the authorized isolation/removal action during a monitoring window, and check RMS for persistent abnormal roster/mapping indicators if readable.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation that the affected workflow can obtain a pair.
Confirmation that AMRs route as intended (not uniformly to hospital lane).
Evidence that operation remained stable during the monitoring window (reported by site).
RMS evidence of abnormal entry absence/no longer active state where readable.
Whether RMS screenshots/details are readable; if not, record as inconclusive technical evidence.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Pairing resumes and operation remains stable during observation; RMS no longer shows the relevant abnormal roster/mapping indicator (where readable).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Pairing remains unavailable, AMRs continue abnormal routing, or RMS still shows the relevant unmapped/abnormal state.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Recovery is only reported administratively without direct operational confirmation; RMS screenshots do not show readable final status details; stability monitoring window is not completed.

linked_primary_procedure.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Inspect WCS/Helix DB to confirm AGV state that would support whether roster/mapping abnormalities persisted after the attempted physical recovery.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: The node is a validation gate and the incident packet lacks readable final RMS values; a SSMS inspection procedure is the closest available candidate to validate state beyond site report. However, the node primarily expects site observation, and the candidate is only loosely aligned to specific pairing restoration validation.
match_gaps: No specific query mapping provided in the packet to correlate validation to the pairing/unable-to-get-a-pair concept.
The node expects RMS and/or site observation; SSMS procedure may not directly show 'pairing availability' without additional zone/workflow mapping.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use the site’s operational confirmation as primary validation, and only use RMS/DB corroboration where data is readable and correlated. Do not close the case solely because a case comment says 'it recovered'—ensure the monitoring window completes and confirm that the abnormal routing behavior no longer appears.

inconclusive_indicators: The source evidence does not identify whether the issue is mechanical, mapping-related, or another subsystem condition.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not infer a confirmed root cause or authorize unsupported database, configuration, or physical actions.

nodes.primary_action: If the supported roster-recovery path is unsafe/unsuccessful or validation does not confirm recovery, prepare an escalation handoff with site-observed symptoms, RMS evidence status (including unreadable portions), physical robot state, actions attempted, authorization/safety constraints, and validation results.
evidence_to_collect: Site-observed pairing and routing symptoms (what is happening now).
RMS screenshots/status evidence and whether key values are unreadable.
Physical robot state (whether isolation/removal occurred and in what safe state).
Actions attempted and what could not be completed safely or within authorization.
Validation results (monitoring window outcome: recovered vs not recovered).
Explicit statement of any ambiguity/inconclusive evidence and missing correlatable identifiers.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Handoff includes all required evidence and stop criteria; a supported continuation exists only when authorization, safety, system-side state, and recovery evidence are sufficient.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Evidence is missing/contradictory, physical safety or authorization cannot be ensured, or pairing/routing did not recover after supported action.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Cannot determine whether the issue is mechanical vs mapping-related vs another subsystem due to insufficient evidence; RMS values are unreadable and cannot be correlated to pairing workflow.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not infer a confirmed root cause. Do not prescribe additional physical steps or database/config changes without safe, validated evidence and proper role boundaries.

ontology_evidence.evidence_text: Stop/escalate when evidence cannot confirm roster/map state or correlates to pairing failure; treat unreadable/un-correlatable evidence as a catalog gap requiring escalation/SME review.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Escalate only with evidence and explicit stop criteria; do not continue with unsupported recovery steps.

nodes.title: Restore the affected AGV sequence or pairing state through an authorized recovery path
nodes.intent: Use an approved, role-authorized recovery procedure to restore the affected AGV or pair to a valid operating sequence when the diagnostic evidence supports that direction.
nodes.goal: Use an approved, role-authorized recovery procedure to restore the affected AGV or pair to a valid operating sequence when the diagnostic evidence supports that direction.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized AGV sequence, pairing, removal, replacement, or controlled return-to-operation recovery, including the requirement that an AGV removed from the grid be appropriately replaced and that safety and role limits be respected; do not infer a specific robot or exact recovery action.
nodes.source_supported_description: Support asked the site to remove and add AGV pairs; the source also states that a removed AGV without a tote must be replaced and later reports robots in proper sequence.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized AGV sequence, pairing, removal, replacement, or controlled return-to-operation recovery, including the requirement that an AGV removed from the grid be appropriately replaced and that safety and role limits be respected; do not infer a specific robot or exact recovery action.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L2 support or another authorized role records that the approved recovery path was completed. Progress evidence is that affected robots remain on, the relevant sequence or pairing state is restored, and bag-out can proceed; failure evidence is continued inactivity, repeated stopping, or an unresolved sequence or pairing condition; inconclusive evidence is that the exact recovery action or resulting state cannot be verified.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support messages directed removal and addition of AGV pairs and discussed restoring robots to proper sequence.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not establish the exact authorized AGV recovery procedure or the decisive action used in this case.
healthy_indicators: Authorized personnel confirm the affected AGV or pair is in the expected sequence.
Robots remain on and available after the approved recovery.
The recovery path reports completion without introducing a new fault.
unhealthy_indicators: The affected AGV or pair remains out of sequence or unavailable.
Robots turn off again or remain unable to support bag-out.
Bag-out starts but stops again after the recovery attempt.
inconclusive_indicators: The source does not identify which action restored service.
The sequence or pairing state cannot be confirmed.
The role authorized to perform the recovery is unavailable.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not proceed with physical or state-changing recovery unless the role, safety conditions, and approved procedure are established.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Asked the site to remove and add AGV pairs; bag-out started, processed most, then stopped.
When all robots were in proper sequence, the customer confirmed they were functional.

nodes.primary_action: Restore the affected AGV sequence/pairing state using an authorized recovery path consistent with the diagnostic evidence; ensure removed AGVs are appropriately replaced and operations are resumed within role/safety limits.
nodes.primary_surface: rms_ui (and physical_floor if the recovery requires on-floor remove/re-add actions, following role boundaries)
evidence_to_collect: Confirmation that the chosen authorized recovery path was completed
Evidence that the affected AGVs/pairs remain in expected operating sequence after recovery
Evidence that bag-out can proceed (no immediate re-stall attributable to the same condition)
Whether recovery introduces a new fault or leaves the sequence/pairing unresolved
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Authorized personnel confirm the affected AGV or pair is in expected sequence; robots remain on and available after recovery; and recovery completion did not introduce a new fault.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Affected AGV/pair remains out of sequence/unavailable; robots turn off again or cannot support bag-out; bag-out starts but stops again after recovery attempt.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The exact decisive recovery action and resulting sequence/pairing state cannot be verified; required authorized role is unavailable.
nodes.generated_guidance: Only execute recovery actions that are consistent with the current diagnostic evidence. If the diagnostic outcome points to AGV sequence/pairing restoration, use an authorized recovery procedure that includes correct replacement/backfill expectations. Do not assume the exact robot/pair details—follow the recovery procedure’s handling for the evidence you identified.

ontology_evidence.evidence: Recovery node requires authorized restore of AGV sequence/pairing via remove/add or related recovery actions plus roster repair expectations.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Authorized recovery is attempted and completion status is verified as healthy/unhealthy/inconclusive.

nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Required evidence surfaces are unavailable/unreadable, decisive recovery action cannot be identified, or fault-to-bag-out relationship remains ambiguous.
nodes.generated_guidance: Escalate when supported recovery completion cannot be verified, validation fails, or the relationship between HMI fault and bag-out stoppage cannot be demonstrated. ontology_evidence.evidence: Escalation is required when overall stoppage evidence cannot be reconciled with recovery/validation outcomes.

playbooks.title: Hospital tote-induct or site-flow disruption with AGV state anomalies
playbooks.user_facing_summary: Use this path when a hospital station cannot add or induct totes, a robot appears shut down, or the site cannot start or sustain sort. Confirm the observable impact, check for AGV location or tote-association anomalies, consider the source-supported service and lane recovery path, and validate tote flow and site operation.
playbooks.playbook_goal: Restore safe hospital tote flow and broader site operation by distinguishing a localized hospital workflow problem from an AGV/tote-state or service-related disruption, applying only authorized high-level recovery actions, and validating stable operation.
observed_entry_symptoms: Hospital station cannot add or induct totes.
Totes can be removed but cannot be added at the hospital area.
A robot or AGV is reported in a shut down state.
The site cannot start sort or goes down during sort.
Hospital backlog or abnormal tote flow to the hospital area is reported.

nodes.intent: Determine whether the current report is an active hospital tote-induct problem, a broader sort disruption, or a localized condition that does not match this response path.

nodes.source_supported_description: The case subject and closure summary describe inability to induct totes, while Teams messages describe inability to add totes and a later site-down or sort-start failure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether totes can be added and removed at the affected hospital station, whether the reported robot or station is shut down, whether sort can start or remain running, and what the Hospital HMI or related HMI view visibly reports.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Site operator or support user confirms the affected workflow through a site interview and, when available, the Hospital HMI or related HMI view. Healthy signal: totes can be added and removed and sort is operating normally. Unhealthy signal: hospital tote addition or induction is unavailable, the station reports a shut down condition, or sort cannot start or sustain operation. Inconclusive: the site cannot identify the affected workflow or the available HMI/status image is unreadable.

healthy_indicators: Site confirms totes can be added and removed at the hospital station.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm with the site and, when available, the Hospital HMI whether totes can currently be added/inducted and removed at the affected hospital station, whether the reported robot/station is in a shut down state, and whether sort can start and remain running.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation (current): can totes be added/inducted at the hospital station?
Site confirmation (current): can totes be removed at the hospital station?

Whether sort can start and whether it stays running (current, not historical)

nodes.healthy_interpretation: Totes can be added/inducted and removed at the hospital station, and sort starts and remains running normally.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital tote addition/induction is unavailable, the station/robot reports a shut down condition, or sort cannot start and/or stops during operation; hospital backlog continues to increase.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The site cannot identify the affected workflow and/or the Hospital HMI/status evidence is unreadable or missing.

optional_corroboration.note: If the site reports shutdown/fault states, corroborate with Hospital HMI alarms and status indicators rather than relying on screenshots with unreadable labels.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Check Hospital HMI Operations Screen Induct/Extract Position Read-Only Data and WCS Status Messages
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Provide a read-only confirmation of whether the Hospital station is accepting induct/extract operations and what status/WCS messages are displayed.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Best lexical/intent match to confirming induct/extract availability and status messages on the Hospital HMI, aligned with node_1’s expected healthy/unhealthy outcomes.

nodes.generated_guidance: First validate the entry criteria in current time: (1) tote add/induct works, (2) tote remove works, (3) station/robot is not in shut down, and (4) sort can start and remain running. If you cannot read the Hospital HMI or the site cannot describe the current workflow behavior, treat as inconclusive and do not jump to AGV/server causes.

nodes.title: Check for AGV location, roster, and tote-association anomalies
nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported hospital-flow problem coincides with an AGV in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy, disconnected tote, or residual tote association.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the reported hospital-flow problem coincides with an AGV in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy, disconnected tote, or residual tote association.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to compare the affected AGV or robot location and rack occupancy with the expected fleet or station state using the source-referenced HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet status view, and API/Aveva state view when available; the procedure should also identify residual or disconnected tote associations without prescribing data mutations.
nodes.source_supported_description: Teams messages and annotated HMI-style images describe an AGV in an unexpected location, two AGVs under a rack, and possible disconnected or residual tote associations.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to compare the affected AGV or robot location and rack occupancy with the expected fleet or station state using the source-referenced HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet status view, and API/Aveva state view when available; the procedure should also identify residual or disconnected tote associations without prescribing data mutations.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Site operator or support user observes the physical or displayed AGV state using the available HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet view when available, and the source-referenced API/Aveva state-management interface. Healthy signal: AGVs occupy expected locations and no disconnected or residual tote association is reported. Unhealthy signal: an AGV is reported in an unexpected location, multiple AGVs appear under one rack or in one location, an AGV is absent from an expected rack, or a disconnected/associated tote remains in the system. Inconclusive: identifiers, locations, or tote associations cannot be confirmed from the available view.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Chat states that Aveva was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station, and that Aveva hits the same endpoints as API dog.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet includes a possible zone/location mismatch, but not a confirmed pairing failure.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a specific backend mapping for the source-described disconnected tote and rack-occupancy evidence.
healthy_indicators: AGVs are shown or confirmed in expected locations.
Expected racks or stations have the expected AGV occupancy.
No disconnected or residual tote association is reported.
The hospital station's displayed tote state is consistent with physical operation.
unhealthy_indicators: AGV is reported not to belong in the displayed location.
Two AGVs appear under the same rack or in the same zone.
A rack or expected location is missing an AGV.
An AGV is associated with a disconnected or residual tote.
Hospital tote state cannot be reconciled with the displayed AGV state.
inconclusive_indicators: AGV identifiers or rack labels are unreadable.
The display is only an annotated image without a reliable legend.
Physical and displayed locations cannot be compared.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: This AGV doesn't belong here; two AGVs were under the rack in the same zone.
AGV with disconnected tote was in the system; other AGVs were under the rack.
Aveva was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station.

nodes.primary_action: Compare the affected hospital/expected AGV locations and station/rack occupancy with the displayed HMI evidence and the system/fleet/API evidence to identify whether anomalies exist (unexpected location, duplicate rack occupancy, missing expected AGV, residual/disconnected tote association).
nodes.primary_surface: rms_ui or wcs_api read-only corroboration + aveva_hmi (as available) + source-referenced hospital/rack view
evidence_to_collect: From source-referenced HMI/layout: whether any AGV/robot appears in an unexpected location relative to the hospital area/rack
Whether two AGVs appear under the same rack/zone or otherwise duplicate occupancy is shown
Whether any expected rack/location is missing an AGV
Whether there is evidence of residual/disconnected tote association (tote state not matching displayed AGV presence)
If HMI identifiers/labels are unreadable, record the inconclusive evidence gap
nodes.healthy_interpretation: AGVs occupy expected locations and no disconnected/residual tote association is reported; hospital station tote state matches physical/operational intent.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: AGVs are in unexpected locations, duplicate rack occupancy appears, an expected rack/location is missing AGV presence, or a disconnected/residual tote association persists; hospital tote state cannot be reconciled with displayed AGV state.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Identifiers/locations/tote associations cannot be confirmed due to unreadable legends or inability to compare physical vs displayed states.

optional_corroboration.note: If you suspect disconnected or residual tote association, corroborate tote presence/association using the most direct read-only screen available; do not proceed to any API/Aveva mutation in this diagnostic node.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Check Hospital HMI Operations Screen Induct/Extract Position Read-Only Data and WCS Status Messages
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Provide read-only Hospital HMI evidence to support whether hospital induct/extract states are consistent with tote presence/association behavior during the anomaly check.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Top candidate list for node_2 did not include a clearly dedicated RMS/WCS/AVEVA tote-association diagnostic procedure; the selected link is the closest read-only Hospital HMI evidence procedure available, but it may not fully cover AGV roster/location anomaly and disconnected tote association.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use a two-part comparison: (1) what the hospital/rack evidence shows about AGV placement and tote state, and (2) what the fleet/system views show about AGV locations and whether tote association is consistent. If you can confirm mismatch/disconnected association, you can select the authorized high-level recovery path next. If you cannot confirm an anomaly, treat service condition as the alternate investigation rather than forcing recovery for an unproven mismatch.

nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service condition is present and sufficiently correlated with the hospital or site-flow symptoms.

nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to review the incident's AGV hospital-station and OptiSweep service evidence, inspect Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services for current service health when access is authorized, and correlate that state with Hospital Lane or HMI responsiveness without assuming that the historical reset note proves a current fault.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source documents AGV hospital-station server issues, a need to reset services, and a closure statement that OptiSweep services were reset before Hospital Lane was restarted.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to review the incident's AGV hospital-station and OptiSweep service evidence, inspect Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services for current service health when access is authorized, and correlate that state with Hospital Lane or HMI responsiveness without assuming that the historical reset note proves a current fault.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1 or L2 support inspects the source-named service evidence in the available work-order or service notes and, where authorized, Windows Event Viewer or Windows Services for the affected host; the site or support user may also confirm Hospital Lane or HMI responsiveness. Healthy signal: the relevant service and hospital interface are responsive and no current abnormal service condition is evident. Unhealthy signal: current evidence shows an AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service abnormality, the hospital interface is unresponsive, or service-reset context coincides with the reported disruption. Inconclusive: the source only contains a historical note saying services need reset, without current status or named service details.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet identifies a Windows-services-related artifact and repeatedly documents AGV hospital-station server issues and a need to reset services, although the visible artifact is a notes pane rather than a live Event Viewer screen.

The packet includes hospital/rack HMI-style screenshots and references Hospital Lane operation.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not identify the exact OptiSweep service names or map the historical service-note artifact to current service-state fields.
healthy_indicators: Authorized support confirms the relevant service is running and responsive.
Hospital Lane or the related HMI responds normally.
No current service abnormality is found.
unhealthy_indicators: Current evidence shows a stopped, repeatedly failing, or otherwise abnormal relevant service.
Hospital Lane or its related HMI remains unresponsive while service health is abnormal.
A current service condition correlates with the inability to induct or start sort.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a historical note says services need reset.
The exact service names or host are not identified.
The available artifact is a notes pane rather than a live service-status view.

nodes.intent: Use the approved recovery procedure appropriate to the confirmed condition: service or lane recovery, correction of supported AGV/tote state, or controlled physical AGV handling.
nodes.goal: Use the approved recovery procedure appropriate to the confirmed condition: service or lane recovery, correction of supported AGV/tote state, or controlled physical AGV handling.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for the authorized recovery path selected from the diagnosis: reset or recover the named OptiSweep or AGV hospital-station services and restart Hospital Lane when approved; alternatively use the approved API dog or Aveva procedure for supported tote or AGV state correction; include site safety controls, role limits, and conditions for any physical AGV removal. Exact commands, click paths, and mutation steps belong in the linked runbook.
nodes.source_supported_description: Historical evidence describes service reset and Hospital Lane restart, API dog removal of tote state, Aveva-based AGV/tote state correction, and removal of several AGVs during recovery. These actions are preserved as high-level source evidence, not procedural instructions.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for the authorized recovery path selected from the diagnosis: reset or recover the named OptiSweep or AGV hospital-station services and restart Hospital Lane when approved; alternatively use the approved API dog or Aveva procedure for supported tote or AGV state correction; include site safety controls, role limits, and conditions for any physical AGV removal. Exact commands, click paths, and mutation steps belong in the linked runbook.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Authorized support or site personnel complete the applicable approved recovery and record whether it completed. Recovery signal: the source-supported service or lane recovery is completed, or the affected AGV/tote state is corrected through the approved API/Aveva or physical procedure. Unsuccessful signal: the action cannot be completed, the state remains abnormal, or the action introduces additional tote or AGV discrepancies. Inconclusive: the source does not identify the exact service, authorization, or safe physical conditions required.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Source notes state that services needed to be reset, and the closure summary states OptiSweep services were reset.

ontology_gaps: The source does not identify the exact OptiSweep services, API operation names, physical isolation requirements, or authorization boundaries for the historical recovery actions.
healthy_indicators: Approved recovery completed and appropriate state restored.
unhealthy_indicators: Recovery unsuccessful; abnormal state persists or new discrepancies appear.
inconclusive_indicators: The recovery action or authorization is not supported by a named procedure.

nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not perform a service reset, API/Aveva state mutation, or physical AGV handling unless the responsible role has an approved procedure and the required safety and authorization conditions are met.

nodes.primary_action: Execute the authorized high-level recovery corresponding to the confirmed condition (either service/lane recovery, or authorized AGV/tote state correction) using the approved procedure; do not perform any unsupported reset or any physical AGV handling unless role limits and safety/authorization conditions are satisfied and the responsible recovery procedure is selected.
nodes.primary_surface: recovery control surfaces per the linked runbook (e.g., WCS API / Apidog and Hospital Lane restart where authorized; or approved AGV/tote operations)
evidence_to_collect: What condition was confirmed by the diagnostic nodes (node_1/node_2/node_3) to select the appropriate approved recovery procedure
